clue.text: Eternal punishment for the mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the motherland deserves to be condemned forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation to hell, the everlasting penalty of the wicked in Christian belief.

clue.text: Shenanigans when social workers get in charge

indicators.note: the workers get, or take inside them, the next abbreviation, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ants are social insects whose sterile members are called workers

explanation.surface: Mischief breaks out when the welfare officers take command.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are playful or silly capers, the same sort of mischief as shenanigans.

clue.text: Gossip to Jack — what a toad!

explanation.surface: Someone tells their friend Jack some gossip about a nasty man, calling him a toad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: put the answer in front of Jack and you get the natterjack, a European toad. The exclamation 'what a toad!' sounds like an insult but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly or gossip; add Jack and it names the natterjack, a small toad with a yellow back stripe.

clue.text: Titchy adolescent going to empty subway

parts.note: a teen is an adolescent

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only the outside letters of subway

explanation.surface: A small teenager heads for a deserted underground passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titchy' is British slang for very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal ways of saying tiny.

clue.text: Expand on work and get two points dismissed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
E and N are two compass points, east and north
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A worker builds on a job only to lose a couple of points.
explanation.definitionFit: To open out is to spread or widen, as a valley or a folded map does, a synonym of expanding.

clue.text: Fish available from one port only

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent, England
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A certain fish is said to be landed at a single harbour and nowhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is England's busiest ferry port, facing France.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a prized European flatfish, named after the port where it was traditionally landed.

clue.text: Mean man to hide stone

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
flint is a hard grey stone

explanation.surface: A stingy fellow tries to conceal a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a miser, someone tight with money.

clue.text: From three sides, pointed at monument to Albert

parts.note: a pyramid is a huge tomb monument, as in Egypt
Al is a short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: Someone, from three angles, gestured at a memorial to a man called Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointed at' reads as aiming a finger, but 'pointed' belongs to the definition and 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramidal describes a shape whose sloping faces rise to a single apex.

clue.text: For Scotsman, vital to be a swinger!

parts.note: mon is the Scots way of saying man
key means essential or vital, as in a key witness

explanation.surface: A Scot is told it is essential to lead a swinging lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkeys swing from branch to branch, so the animal is playfully called a swinger.

clue.text: A worthy man spoke, but not fluently

definitions.text: A worthy man spoke, but not fluently

parts.note: a saint is a holy, worthy person, abbreviated ST
uttered means spoke

explanation.surface: A good man gives a speech, though haltingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: a saint who spoke, though not smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stutter is to speak with involuntary repetitions and pauses.

clue.text: Objective woman in a pickle causing a rupture

parts.note: her is the objective form of she, a woman's pronoun

indicators.note: being in a pickle means being in a mess, so the two little words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman in a tricky spot does herself an internal injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' looks like a single phrase, but 'in a' is the fodder and 'pickle' alone signals the rearrangement to NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is the protrusion of an organ through a tear or weakness in muscle wall.

clue.text: Coming into office entrance, see no-one has returned

parts.note: access means a way in, an entrance

indicators.note: returned means the letters for no and one come back in the opposite direction

parts.note: no gives NO and one gives I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A new office holder finds the doorway deserted and nobody back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has returned' turns NO plus I (one) round to ION. 'see' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accession is the taking up of a high post, as a monarch's accession to the throne.

clue.text: A condiment I use in fits and starts

parts.note: salt is a condiment for seasoning food

explanation.surface: Someone sprinkles a seasoning irregularly over their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A salti' is a musical term borrowed from Italian, meaning by leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means by jumps, so it describes something done jerkily and intermittently.

clue.text: They've forgotten man's case, I suspect

indicators.note: a suspect version is doubtful and not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of man's, taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective admits a fellow's legal case is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' sounds like a detective's hunch, but 'suspect' tells you to rearrange MANS, CASE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesiacs are people suffering memory loss.

clue.text: Find fault with fruit and get a different one

definitions.note: one stands for a fruit, so the definition is another kind of fruit

parts.note: to crab is to criticise or grumble about
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone criticises their fruit and swaps it for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'fruit': the answer is another fruit, built from the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crab apple is a small sour wild relative of the eating apple, so another fruit altogether.

clue.text: A reasonable amount to pay out on Capri fire disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of the island and the blaze are thrown into new order

explanation.surface: Someone shells out an acceptable sum after a blaze on an Italian island.
explanation.walkthrough: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair price is a sum that is just and not excessive for what is bought.

clue.text: Wartime servicewomen find a way back

indicators.note: back means the letters of the abbreviation for way are read the other way round

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Women in uniform during the war search for a route home.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army branch in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The ATS was the women's branch of the British Army during the Second World War.

clue.text: Snake could spring out

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word for spring are put out of order

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A snake might leap forth suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring out' reads as a snake striking, but 'spring' is SPA and 'out' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a venomous snake, the Egyptian cobra of Cleopatra's legend.

clue.text: Aversion to winter making one blue

explanation.surface: A dislike of the cold season leaves someone low in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is the abbreviation for seasonal affective disorder, depression brought on by winter's short days.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal affective disorder is winter-linked low mood, and feeling blue means being unhappy.

clue.text: People who don't go on interminably

definitions.text: People who don't go on interminably

parts.words: People who don't go on interminably
parts.note: reads as people who don't talk endlessly, but means beings who do not live forever

explanation.definitionFit: Humans are subject to death, unlike the immortal gods.

clue.text: Legendary runner loses second race in Georgia

indicators.note: the runner's name loses its second A, which comes third

parts.note: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek myth who raced her suitors

explanation.surface: A mythical sprinter is beaten in a second race in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' may hint at Atalanta's famous footrace; the city of Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: A pack of peas

parts.note: reads as a supermarket bag of frozen peas, but means the natural case peas grow in

explanation.definitionFit: Peas grow inside a long green seed case, nature's own packaging.

clue.text: At first viewing it's hot sign-posting!

indicators.note: posting suggests sending off or moving, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A notice warns of heat on a signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign-posting' looks like one word, but 'sign' ends the fodder HOT SIGN and 'posting' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on sight means doing it immediately when first seen, as in shoot on sight.

clue.text: They're smouldering in "September song"

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the two quoted words, across the gap

explanation.surface: A singer mentions glowing coals in the lyrics of a well-known autumnal ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'September Song' is a famous popular standard, a nostalgic piece about the fading year.
explanation.definitionFit: Embers are glowing remnants of a fire still burning without flame.

clue.text: Old filmstar Deborah had one, a deciduous shrub

parts.note: Deborah Kerr was a Scottish-born actress of the 1940s and 50s
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A classic screen actress owned a particular garden bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerria is a Japanese shrub with yellow flowers that drops its leaves in autumn.

clue.text: For instance, seabird goes towards back of ship

parts.note: as means for instance, as in sports such as tennis
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull-like bird flies to the stern of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for at or towards the rear of a boat.

clue.text: Rule over borders of first great nation

indicators.note: the initials of the next two words border, or sit either side of, the word over
first means take the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: over taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler extends control over the frontiers of the leading world power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of 'Rule over', but it is the letters OVER, enclosed by G and N, the first letters of 'great' and 'nation'.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule a country or people.

clue.text: Like Iranian said, it's slander

indicators.note: said means the phrase for like an Iranian is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: as means like, and an Iranian is a Persian

explanation.surface: Someone claims a remark about an Iranian is defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As Persian', spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to make damaging remarks about someone, so the word means a defamatory slur.

clue.text: I'm having a post-prandial tipple — bring it in!

parts.note: port is a fortified wine drunk after dinner

explanation.surface: A diner asks for a glass of something after the meal and for it to be fetched.
explanation.definitionFit: To import is to bring goods into a country from abroad.

clue.text: Distressed by old, confused giver-in

indicators.note: in means the muddled letters go inside the word for old

parts.note: aged means old

indicators.note: confused means the letters of giver are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by an elderly, muddled person who gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giver-in' reads as one word for a quitter, but the hyphen hides two jobs: 'giver' is the fodder for 'confused', and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggrieved means feeling wronged and resentful, hurt by unfair treatment.

clue.text: Material produced by the California island company

explanation.surface: A fabric is made by a firm on a Californian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton cloth, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Over-exerting by exercising on the Sabbath?

indicators.note: on means the word for exercising is placed after the abbreviation

parts.note: S is a dictionary abbreviation for Sabbath
training means exercising

explanation.surface: Someone works out too hard on their day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: S for Sabbath is listed in Chambers but is uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining means making a great or excessive effort.
